entities.summary:
Ban Biao (3–54 CE) was a pivotal figure in Chinese historiography during the Eastern Han dynasty, whose intellectual legacy profoundly shaped the official historical record of the preceding Western Han. Born in Xianyang, a city with deep historical roots, into an aristocratic and scholarly family, he served as an official under Emperor Guangwu. His ambition was to rectify perceived shortcomings in Sima Qian's *Records of the Grand Historian* regarding the Han period, specifically aiming to create a comprehensive, single-dynasty history that would later become the standard for imperial Chinese historiography. His pioneering efforts established the thematic and structural framework for the *Book of Han* (Hanshu), an indispensable source for the study of China's classical age.

Serving in various capacities, including as an official in the commanderies of Shu and Kuaiji, Ban Biao dedicated a substantial portion of his life to scholarship, particularly the compilation of historical records. He perceived that Sima Qian's *Shiji*, while groundbreaking, treated the Han dynasty merely as a continuation of previous imperial cycles, rather than as a distinct entity deserving its own dedicated chronicle. Ban Biao thus began compiling the *Later Traditions* (Houzhuan), a work designed to extend and refine the historical narrative specifically for the Western Han period. This project, though unfinished at his death in 54 CE, meticulously gathered source materials, organized narratives, and established a chronological and thematic structure that proved invaluable.
